reviewBoundary: Three complete junior fifteen-gap/four-choice narratives. Fictional recording, glove-recovery and library-audio cases. Same-author key/all-alternative review, not independent calibration.

materials.title: The bell in the recording
materials.text:
For a class sound-recording task, I chose our local church bell. I had heard it every day, but never really ____1____ to it.

Dad joined me at the square before noon. The first bell sounded clearly, then a delivery van stopped nearby with its engine ____2____. I stopped the recording in disappointment.

Dad reminded me that ordinary sounds need not sound like studio performances.  I could keep the recording and ____3____ what was happening, rather than pretend the bell existed in an empty place.

I made a second recording from farther away. The engine was quieter there, but the bell sounded less ____4____ too. A third clip caught birds and a bicycle.

At school, I played the first version. A classmate recognised the van before the bell. It was the van that ____5____ parcels to her family’s shop. Another student noticed that the sound returned faintly after each strike, as it reflected from nearby buildings.

We listened without trying to remove every ____6____ sound from our attention. The short clip became a picture of a place, though it had no ____7____ image.

For my notes, I wrote the time, date and position of the phone. They would help me ____8____ a later recording. I did not call the engine an error; it was something that actually ____9____ during the chosen minute.

The teacher combined rain, door, footstep and bell clips. The result was not a real journey through town, but a new ____10____ made from real sounds. We did not call it a documentary. I still liked the clear bell, but the ____11____ around it had become interesting too. On the walk home, I heard a similar van and looked up. This time, the ordinary engine did not feel like an ____12____ to listening. It was one more thing to ____13____. I could decide what to focus on without ____14____ that everything else was absent. Even a familiar sound had a ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Listened to means attended to sound. Spoken/written/paid do not express hearing attention.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A running engine adds noise. Missing/silent would not obscure the bell; no breakdown is stated.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: He can describe the van context. Denying/forgetting hides it and selling does not document it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Distance reduces the bell’s clarity. Cost/age/weight do not change with recording position.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The delivery van delivers at that shop. Sleeping/studying/swimming do not describe its work.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Other sounds surround the bell. Future/written/silent do not describe audible context in the clip.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A sound recording has no visual image. Quiet/musical/distant do not distinguish image from audio.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Conditions allow comparison with a later recording. Cancellation/printing/hiding do not examine differences.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The engine was an event that happened. Vanished would mean disappearance, cost needs an amount and promised implies intent.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Edited real sounds form a new composition. It is explicitly not a real journey, nor a physical location or engine.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The surrounding audio is now interesting. Colours/tickets/numbers are not what the listener hears.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: It no longer blocks listening, an obstacle. Invitation/answer/address do not name the interference originally perceived.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Notice means attend to the real sound. Buying/painting/inventing do not describe observation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: He avoids assuming other sounds are absent. Showing/hearing/checking would require evidence rather than erase reality by supposition.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Setting is the surrounding situation revealed by the clip. Cost/name/ticket do not describe the acoustic context.

materials.title: Gloves on the line
materials.text:
After the winter fair, our class found a box of gloves left in the hall. Some were pairs, but many had lost their ____1____. We helped return them.

We first arranged them by colour. That did not show whether two gloves were the same ____2____. A tiny blue glove could not be paired with a much larger blue one simply because their colour matched.

Hana suggested a line and clips. We left space between them so that visitors could ____3____ each glove. Searching no longer meant emptying the box.

Then we wrote a notice for families. It gave the display place and supervised times. We did not put children's names on the gloves unless the owners were already ____4____. A guess could send the wrong item home.

On Monday, a father found one red glove and smiled. His daughter had kept the other one in her coat pocket. She held it beside ours to ____5____. They matched, and she took the pair.

Another child pointed to a black glove but was unsure. The teacher asked her to ____6____ it before taking it down. She remembered a small silver button near the wrist. That helped distinguish it from two similar ones.

By Wednesday, most gloves had gone. We kept the remaining items in lost property and removed the outdoor ____7____ before rain arrived. The class did not throw away things simply because nobody had claimed them ____8____.

 The task had required us to think about the person trying to ____9____ something.  Giving each glove a visible place had made the ____10____ easier. The teacher kept our clips for another event, but we changed the label on the box to "display clips". Otherwise, next year’s class might ____11____ the help they needed. Hana drew a tiny peg on the label. I added "Not gloves!", but we decided the first label was ____12____. Too many words could make a simple sign harder to ____13____. The box went onto the cupboard shelf, ready for ____14____. We had finished returning gloves, but the equipment could still be ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Unpaired gloves lack their matching partners. Fingers/colours/prices do not name the other glove.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Tiny and larger blue gloves differ in size. Colour already matches; day/owner alone does not describe dimensions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Separated hanging display makes each visible. Wearing/buying/washing are not its search function.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Names are used only when ownership is known. Timing/temperature/height do not establish it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: She compares the retained glove with the found one. The other verbs do not check matching pattern/size.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Describing a remembered button identifies it. Buying/knitting/borrowing do not verify ownership.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: They remove the outdoor display before rain. Weather/cupboard/teacher are not the hung arrangement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Not claimed yet allows later recovery. Never makes a permanent claim and the other phrases do not fit the temporal meaning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The owner searches to find a lost item. Painting/teaching/invention are unrelated to retrieval.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Visible positions make searching easier. Winter/knitting/price are not the activity improved by arrangement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Mistaking contents could cause the next class to miss available clips/help. Provide/offer/accept do not mean fail to notice.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: They decide the original label is enough. Missing/wrong/wet do not explain removing redundant added words.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Too much text can make a sign harder to read. The other actions concern the object, not its message.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Keeping the clips readies reuse. Rubbish/sale are not planned and not every future event is winter.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Saved equipment remains useful after the glove task. Lost/empty/borrowed do not describe its retained purpose.

materials.title: The staircase in the story
materials.text:
Lena practised a story for the library’s audio collection until the words sounded ____1____. The librarian asked a new listener to help.

Her friend Amir followed easily until the main character climbed a staircase. Lena had read faster and faster to create ____2____. Amir thought the character was running, but the next paragraph described a slow, careful search.

Lena checked the page. The staircase scene contained no instruction to hurry. She had added that feeling because she knew what would happen ____3____. 

She tried the passage again at a steadier pace. This time Amir noticed the sound of a door opening halfway up. It had been ____4____ in the earlier rush, though Lena had spoken every word correctly.

The librarian suggested marking the page with small pauses, not changing the author's sentences. Lena could make the structure easier to hear without ____5____ the plot. Her pencil marks could be revised.

Recording day brought a different problem: a chair made a loud sound whenever she moved. They stopped and changed chairs rather than hoping the noise would ____6____ in the final file. The volunteer checked a test clip.

When Lena listened back, her own voice sounded strange. The volunteer asked her to focus on the ____7____: could a listener follow what happened? Feeling strange did not prove the recording unusable.

The finished file included a clear title and the reader's name. The library had permission to use the story and recorded that ____8____ with the file. Good reading still needed arrangements for public ____9____.

At the launch, Amir smiled at the staircase scene. Lena had not made the story more ____10____ by adding speed everywhere. She had made its own changes in pace easier to ____11____. Afterwards, another volunteer asked for advice. Lena did not offer a single perfect reading ____12____. She suggested finding an unfamiliar listener. A familiar page could hide a ____13____ from its reader. Giving it to new ears was one way to ____14____ it. Then she borrowed an audiobook herself and enjoyed, for once, being the ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Practice makes delivery fluent. Distance/silence/cost do not describe smooth spoken words.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Increasing speed creates excitement/tension. Silence/permission/evidence are not that performance feeling.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: She knows later plot events, next. Location/past day/solitude do not identify story sequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The door sound’s significance was lost in rushed delivery. Words were spoken, so printing/repetition/announcement do not name missed perception.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: She changes delivery without altering plot. Following/reading/remembering are compatible with the work and not the prohibited modification.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: They cannot hope recorded chair noise will simply disappear. Increase/return/begin would not solve it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The question concerns listeners following events, meaning. Furniture/price/age do not measure narrative intelligibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Authorization for use is permission recorded with the file. Performance/stairs/speed do not establish rights.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Public access to audio needs permission. Silence/ownership transfer/complaint are not ordinary availability.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Lena avoids making everything dramatic through speed. Accuracy/familiarity/privacy are not the heightened performance effect.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Audio pace changes must be heard. Printing/ownership/hiding do not describe the listener’s experience.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: She avoids one universal formula for reading. A library/permission/room is not a method offered as advice.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Familiarity can hide a comprehension difficulty. A bookshop/payment/chair is not the narrative problem noticed by new ears.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: New listening can discover the existing difficulty. Creating/selling/cancelling is not the diagnostic aim.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Borrowing a book to enjoy others’ work makes her the listener in this audio context. She is not its author, librarian or fictional character.
